requirements.requirement: On node1, only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs.
requirements.summary: The final allowlist contains exactly root and opsadmin, with root-only permissions. Direct tests before and after restart show both permitted users can install crontabs while alpine is rejected. Cronie is installed, running, and enabled at boot.

overall_summary: The requested cron access control is satisfied and remains functional after a verified node restart. Operational hygiene is materially reduced because testing left the package-managed root crontab missing, plus a minor temporary reboot log residue.
limitations: OpenRC service health was directly checked, but the supplemental failed-service collector only supports systemd and therefore could not provide a global failed-service inventory.
Denial was functionally tested with alpine rather than every local account; the exact two-entry cron.allow and representative denial provide strong supporting coverage.

operational_hygiene.summary: The implementation works, and the mandatory restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/configuration/authorization behavior were directly observed and independently corroborated. However, verification unnecessarily overwrote and then removed the pre-existing package-managed /etc/crontabs/root instead of preserving and restoring it; this damage remained in final package health. The responsible test/cleanup actions were cmd-754917b34f0b4af2, cmd-d5ed841113244ff6, and the repeated post-restart test in cmd-cc3193b002b84b6b. A small reboot log created by cmd-94d8a0d6b3474efd also remained under /tmp. No other unnecessary mutations are evident from the timeline.
